subject: Help me understand why this is happening

messages.author: 0862b7ebd66e06c4
messages.subject: Help me understand why this is happening
parts:
I'm trying to learn ggplot2. To help me learn, I'm using an
interesting tiny dataset from
http://ajayshahblog.blogspot.com/2009/05/decline-of-left.html

I find this yields a fascinating plot:

----------------------
library(MASS)
dates <- c(57,62,67,71,77,80,84,89,91,96,98,99,104,109)+1900
vshare <- c(8.9,9.9,9.4,9.8,7.1,8.7,8.6,9.1,8.7,8.1,6.9,6.9,7.1,6.8)
post1991 <- dates > 1991
tmp <- data.frame(dates=dates, vshare=vshare, post1991=post1991)

ggplot(tmp, aes(dates, vshare, colour=factor(post1991))) +
layer(geom="point") +
layer(geom="smooth", method="rlm") +
labs(x=NULL, y="Communist vote share (per cent)")
-------------------------

where the post1991 factor is being used to split the data into two
groups, and rlm() is being used on them separately.

A tiny change to the code gives:

-----------------------
ggplot(tmp, aes(dates, vshare)) +
layer(geom="point", colour=factor(post1991)) +
layer(geom="smooth", method="rlm") +
labs(x=NULL, y="Communist vote share (per cent)")
------------------------

which is a single rlm() over the entire dataset, and the post1991
factor only matters in changing the colour scheme.

I am not able to understand why this tiny change is doing so much.
Could you please explain?

--
Ajay Shah

http://ajayshahblog.blogspot.com

messages.author: 7e54aa65e5af5819
messages.subject: Re: Help me understand why this is happening
parts:
In your first example you are mapping the plot's default colour to
factor(post1991), and all the layers would use this mapping. In the
second example there is no default colour mapping, but instead only
the colour mapping on the points layer.

--
http://learnr.wordpress.com/

parts:
Most importantly in the second example you're setting the colour, not
mapping it - you need aes(colour = factor(post1991))
